title: Creating Classes and Objects
learning_outcomes: Explain what creating classes and objects contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: class declarations.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. In this lesson, focus on class declarations; then compare it with instantiation. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use creating classes and objects when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object-oriented code groups state and behavior. Classes should protect their invariants, expose a clear public API, and use inheritance only when the subtype relationship is meaningful. For creating classes and objects, begin with class declarations. Also distinguish instantiation; properties and methods; object member access. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Creating Classes and Objects
content_blocks.code:
<?php
class Counter { private int $value = 0; public function increment(): void { $this->value++; } public function value(): int { return $this->value; } }
$c = new Counter(); $c->increment();
echo $c->value() . PHP_EOL;

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
